office_does: The sheriff runs the Island County Sheriff's Office: patrol deputies, arrests, service of court papers and the county jail. The sheriff is also county fire marshal and sets burn bans.
race_blurb: Two-term Sheriff Rick Felici, elected as a Republican and now running with an independent preference, faces Langley police chief and former county deputy Tavier Wasser (Prefers Democratic Party). Felici led the primary 51.7% to 48.1%; endorsements cross party lines, and both candidates say deputy coverage is too thin amid a tight county budget.

candidates.summary: Island County sheriff since 2018, with the office since 1994 as deputy, detective, sergeant and chief criminal deputy; seeking a third term with an independent party preference.
highlights: 38 years in law enforcement; sheriff since 2018 [S1]
Calls drugs and mental health the top challenges and wants 'education, enforcement and accountability' [S3]
Points to body cameras, de-escalation training and co-responder mental health and opioid outreach [S1][S11]
Says he will follow the Keep Washington Working Act and rejects the constitutional sheriff movement [S3][S6]
Endorsed by the county Republican Party, the deputies' and corrections unions and Indivisible Whidbey [S4]

experience.basis: Two-term sitting sheriff with 32 years in the office, endorsed by both of its unions.

safety.basis: Frames drugs and mental health around enforcement and accountability and has sought more deputies, while running grant-funded co-responder mental health and opioid outreach.

candidates.summary: Langley police chief since 2022, an Island County deputy and acting sergeant from 2015 to 2022, and a Marine Corps military policeman before that; first run for office.
highlights: Langley police chief since 2022; county deputy 2015-2022 [S1]
Plan: more deputy training, better communication, stronger mental health support and victim advocacy [S6]
Would route some calls, such as behavioral health crises, to social workers [S7]
Proposes a victim advocacy unit and a public information officer [S4][S1]
Says he will follow the Keep Washington Working Act and has repudiated the 'constitutional sheriff' label [S7][S8]

experience.basis: First-time candidate challenging a two-term incumbent, though he has run a small city department since 2022 and served seven years as a county deputy.

safety.basis: Emphasizes expanded mental-health capacity, telling crimes from calls for help, sending some behavioral-health calls to social workers and victim advocacy, alongside more tactical training.
